content.text:
I submitted index 1 (Ca 0.137, Fe 0.701, Mn 0.162) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was only 1×10⁻⁸ A, a very weak signal. With just 3 of 183 compositions measured, I can't say how close this is to the library's best.

**How I chose the three photocurrent measurements:** I used 4 of the 5 X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements to see which crystal phases were present in each corner of the library.
- **Everywhere:** every sample showed the same main phase, a simple cubic (rock-salt-like) oxide.
- **Fe-rich region (index 1):** had extra peaks that fit hematite (Fe₂O₃). Hematite absorbs light at the 2.4 eV used here, so this region looked most promising.
- **Mn-rich region (index 131):** had a different extra phase, probably a manganese oxide.
- **Ca-rich (index 110) and middle (index 24) regions:** showed mainly the common phase. Index 24 had only faint traces of hematite.

**Photocurrent results:**

| Index | Composition (Ca/Fe/Mn) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.14 / 0.70 / 0.16 | +1×10⁻⁸ A (best) |
| 4 | 0.22 / 0.66 / 0.12 | ≈ 0 A |
| 131 | 0.12 / 0.15 / 0.72 | −4×10⁻⁸ A (no useful anodic response) |

**Caveats:**
- All three values are tiny, so none of these samples is a strong photoanode. The +1×10⁻⁸ A could be noise.
- Two regions got no photocurrent measurement: the calcium-rich compositions, and those near a 1:2 Ca:Fe ratio (where a calcium ferrite phase might form). A better sample could be there.
